newsitem.title: USA: U.S. West Coast prods mixed, contradict NYMEX.
newsitem.headline: U.S. West Coast prods mixed, contradict NYMEX.

text.p: Prices for U.S. West Coast products contradicted futures markets, with gasoline weaker and distillates rising in listless trade.
Most traders attended an industry function which runs through to Friday, brokers said.
"I haven't heard anything getting done all day," one broker said. Brokers surveyed by Reuters said they expected few deals to be done until next week.
A slide in fourth quarter margins -- which analysts said fell 21 percent in recent weeks -- have kept refiners from paying up to sellers' levels recently, brokers said.
Sellers, watching a recent uptrend in NYMEX crude and heating oil, have been reluctant to lower offers, creating a trade impasse.
Cash offers for CARB conventional gasoline in Los Angeles slipped a quarter-cent to 67.75, while bids held at 67 cents.
Conventional regular gasoline eased 0.50-1.00 cent after an idle morning, ending 62.50/63.25 cents a gallon Thursday.

NYMEX gasoline for November delivery settled 1.06-cents higher at 69.22 cents a gallon. But NYMEX heating oil fell as traders sold heavily ito buy gasoline. Front-month "heat" ended the day 0.47 lower at 70.49 cents a gallon.
West Coast distillate prices edged up, reacting to rumours that several Los Angeles refiners had failed to make products up to standard.
"There are rumours of off-specification products at three refiners," a broker said. "They might have to go out and buy from someone else if they need to," he said.
Offers for low sulphur diesel rose a half cent to 70/71.50 cents a gallon.
Bids for CARB diesel also rose, hitting 80.50 cents gallon after a 0.50-cent climb from Wednesday.
A maintenance closure of Chevron's Los Angeles fluid catalytic cracker mid-October may also strap prompt supplies, traders said.
Los Angeles jet fuel was flat at at 70.50/71.50 cents a gallon in late trade.
